title.narrative: Fragile States in Africa supported to realize social justice, peace and stability by addressing the underlying causes

description.narrative:
Several African countries face converging crises, including conflict, fragility, climate change, disasters and economic shocks, often leading to forced displacement. These challenges contribute to significant decent work deficits—particularly in rural areas—while unemployment, informality and inequality further exacerbate vulnerability. Promoting decent work across the Humanitarian–Development–Peace Nexus (HDPN) is critical to strengthening resilience and enabling sustainable recovery.
Building on progress achieved during the 2024–2025 biennium, this initiative strengthens the capacity of ILO tripartite constituents to prevent, respond to and recover from crises, in line with ILO Recommendation No. 205 on Employment and Decent Work for Peace and Resilience (2017). R205 recognizes that crises affect poverty and development, human rights and dignity, decent work and sustainable enterprises. It supports the design and implementation of inclusive, rights-based and results-oriented interventions that promote employment, resilient livelihoods and sustainable enterprises in fragile and crisis contexts.
This Regional Outcome enhances constituents’ capacity to advance decent work across all phases of crisis management and promotes integrated approaches linking humanitarian, development and peace efforts. It also supports the production and dissemination of knowledge on the rural economy to inform evidence-based policies and programmes.
